A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison; relocated and renumbered content can be matched.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data simulations, including prediction risks, total variation and sampling runtimes in Section 4 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation results in Section 4 and Appendix I, including the sampling comparison in Table 2.

M1.justification: The generator-matching ERM objective, posterior-parameterized rates, ReLU models, early stopping and uniformization algorithm are unchanged. The efficient-sampler extensions discussed in v3 are prospective directions.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic blockwise AR(1) discrete-data task. No dataset, domain or distinct evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Uniformization and the tau-leaping algorithm attributed to Campbell et al. (2022) remain the same evaluated comparison in v2 Table 1 and v3 Table 2. The expanded discussion of Su et al. is theoretical positioning, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The sample sizes, dimension and early-stopping sweeps, training settings, prediction-risk evaluation, first-three-coordinate total variation metric and 100-interval sampling protocols are unchanged between Appendices H and I.

E4.justification: Both retain the same sensitivity analyses for sample size, dimension and early stopping, plus the sampling accuracy/runtime comparison. No new ablation, robustness test or case study is reported.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All four plots retain their data, and every numerical entry in v2 Table 1 matches v3 Table 2. For example, at D=3 and tau=0.03, total variation remains 0.0551 for uniformization and 0.0561 for tau-leaping. The reported empirical trends are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 3 removes the M_tau multiplier from the approximation bound. Appendix G.3 replaces v2 Appendix F.3's linear bound with a quadratic argument using D_F(a||b) <= (a-b)^2/b. Correspondingly, Equation 13 changes its tau prefactor from tau^(-2) to tau^(-1), and Theorem 5 changes from tau^(-1) to tau^(-1/2). This substantively strengthens a main convergence guarantee under the same assumptions; the fast-rate theorem is unchanged.

C1.justification: The conclusion qualifies the general guarantee as avoiding 'strong conditions,' where v2 said it imposed no conditions on oracle rates and data distributions. This modestly softens that claim; the abstract and introduction retain the same principal contributions and near-optimal fast-rate claim.

C2.justification: New Remark 2 interprets the bounds as guidance for network width, depth and clipping. Section 6 adds specific limitations concerning omitted optimization error and limited guidance for large systems, and discusses possible regularity or masked-source routes to efficient sampling. v2's shorter future-work discussion did not provide these qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix H becomes Appendix I with the same implementation information: four 256-unit ReLU hidden layers, Adam at 1e-3, batch size 512, 2000D/3 training epochs and identical sampling specifications. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: New Remark 4 expands the comparison with the already-cited Su et al. (2025), emphasizing dimension/vocabulary dependence and treatment of early stopping, and relates the slow and fast rates to continuous-flow analyses. v2 mentioned Su et al. only briefly. The cited-work membership is unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order are retained. Local additions include explanatory remarks, a limitations discussion, a notation appendix, acknowledgements and an impact statement, alongside affiliation corrections and citation-style changes.

P2.justification: The single-column main text and references become a two-column conference layout, with running headers and extensive equation and figure reflow. The four existing plots are reordered and relocated. A notation table is added as Table 1, while the unchanged empirical table becomes Table 2.

improvement.justification: The explicit quadratic Bregman bound improves the approximation argument and supports tighter bounds in Theorems 3 and 5. The notation table and specific discussion of optimization error make the theory easier to navigate and its practical scope clearer. These are focused improvements in rigor and interpretation; the empirical evidence and main fast-rate analysis remain unchanged.
